blockers.description: This is conditional: it blocks only if Codex v2 diverges on this axis. CDR-010 pins the reducer, grouping, block sums and predicate, but not element-wise squaring. On glibc 2.39, Python d**2 (libm pow) is not correctly rounded for about 0.085% of doubles (2552/3,000,000, all checked against the exact square). d*d and NumPy arr**2, which approved run() uses, are correctly rounded. v1 and the GIE-008c probe use **2. The two readings change T bits in 12/12 E-SQUARE cases (43 of 106,509 random searches) and t bits in 741 of 106,509. r and p never changed. A pow-based v2 would be libm-version dependent. The oracle default is mul.
blockers.owner: Primary Integration Writer (route); user / Track C register (decide)
blockers.unblock: Pin squaring as multiplication (run()/NumPy semantics) or as pow. Otherwise accept that a v2 matching only variant:square_pow is equivalent on r/deg/p but not on T bits. compare_v2 labels this as matches_reference=variant:square_pow.

blockers.description: This is conditional: it blocks only if Codex v2 uses the other reading. '(Σ full block sums + partial)/n' can be read as fsum(full)+partial, which is the oracle default and matches the GIE-008 §2 'fsum / blocks' column cited by CDR-010 and the run() structure. It can also be read as fsum(full+[partial]). The second reading changes p in 16/648 random cases and r/deg/ties in 21 cases, including the TIE fixture, where ties go from 3 to 2 while p stays .45.
blockers.owner: Primary Integration Writer (route); user if v2 chose the other reading
blockers.unblock: Confirm that the CDR-010 routing record's reference to the GIE-008 §2 column fixes fsum(full)+partial, or have the user pin it. compare_v2 labels a divergence as variant:partial_single_fsum.

findings_nonblocking: F3 (contract silent; any guard would be USER_DECISION_REQUIRED for Track C): with an undefined or near-undefined statistic, literal run() returns the minimum p = 1/(B+1) in all 6 E-UNDEF/NEARUNDEF cases, either because TS = nan or because cumsum residue makes T huge. CDR-010 returns UNDEFINED on 5/6 and v1 raises MissingStatisticalEvidence on 5/6. compare_v2 reports these cases without grading them.

F4 (pre-existing in frozen v1, synthetic only): superiority.studentized_cbb @ b9e01a9 raises ZeroDivisionError when 0 < v and v/n underflows (subnormal inputs around 2^-540). All 10 E-SUBNORMAL cases hit it. It fails closed by exception rather than through MissingStatisticalEvidence. v1 must stay unmodified (CDR-006), so this is recorded only.

F5: exact arithmetic is not a neutral referee. In the random battery, exact decimal and exact binary disagree with each other and with float CDR-010 (exact decimal differs on 49/648 p values, exact binary on 40/648). Most of this is in decimal_zero_mean, where the decimal T is exactly 0 and the float T is a few ulps away; exact-decimal p differs in 41/72 of those cases. Disagreement with exact decimal on these cases is expected under the float fsum contract and is not a v2 defect.

The predicate axis is discriminated: on the 10 E-SUBNORMAL cases a v>0 predicate changes deg in 10/10 and would divide by zero. The grouping axis changes p in 37 cases, including SEED275 (.55 vs .50). Literal run() differs in p on 63 cases, including FLIP. The battery therefore detects every pinned CDR-010 axis.
